builds.howItPlays: You park cheap blockers like Overzealous Fan, a 2-cost unit you can kill while it defends to send an attacker back to its base, on one battlefield, and you stun, bounce or counter whatever your opponent sends at it. Each turn you hold that spot, Vex draws you a card, and Sona, Harmonious readies up to 4 of your runes at the end of your turn, so you still have answers to play on theirs.
builds.whyYou: You like sitting back, watching what your opponent does, and having the right answer ready when they commit to something. You don't mind a slow start as long as you pick one battlefield, make it very hard to take, and draw more cards than the other player every turn you keep it. Most of your points come from holding, not attacking. If patience and a strong finish feel better to you than a fast win, this Vex suits you.

builds.howItPlays: You play 16 to 20 copies of Spiderling, a 3-cost unit that gets +1 Might for each other Spiderling at the same battlefield, setting them face down there for 1 rune each and flipping them in for free later, even on your opponent's turn. The stack grows into one wall that holds for points while Back Off and counterspells protect it, and at The Grand Plaza, a battlefield that wins you the game when you hold it with 7 or more units, Flurry of Feathers can add four 1-Might Birds to reach the count.
builds.whyYou: You like building a deck around one strange idea and watching it work. With most of your deck being the same card, you almost always draw what you need; the skill is in choosing where to hide your Spiderlings and when to flip them in, so your opponent attacks into a pile that suddenly gets huge. One card that answers several units at once can undo a few turns of setup, and you accept that for games where the stack simply can't be beaten. If a single unusual plan that grows stronger every turn sounds fun, this Vex suits you.
builds.ratingNotes: New 2026-09-25 (re-rate from the deck picks, style Spiderling Swarm Vex). Coordinates 4.5/4.5/8/5.5 (pace/stance/complexity/variance) are the mean of three scored decks from tools.ts style. The label is Combo, given by all three raters. On every sheet the scorer suggested Control, because 12 to 16 cards are answers. The raters overrode it because those answers are counters and dodges (Defy, Emperor's Divide, Not So Fast, Hard Bargain, Back Off) that protect the stack, and the plan runs through one engine card. Scored decks: VEX BUT I PUT 20 COPIES OF THE SAME CARD IN (MipZ; 6 likes, video; 20 Spiderling; Bandle Tree, The Grand Plaza, Trifarian War Camp) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/6524967d-1d8d-41c6-affe-0d63c1ccc6f8 Combo 4.5/5/8/6. Vexpider-man (tachu; guide, matchups, pre-ban; 16 Spiderling on the fetched page; Bandle Tree, The Grand Plaza, Power Nexus) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/6ff5ae55-6bdf-463c-afc8-1e8a85aa7466 Combo 4.5/4.5/8/6. Vex Spiders (total; 1 like, pre-ban; Bandle Tree, Trifarian War Camp) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/11ed34e2-bbee-48f4-87b4-ea54d3ace2c6 Combo 4.5/4/8/4.5. Adjustments: Complexity +0.5 on all three, because Bandle Tree lets you hide a second card and Power Nexus adds a when-to-buy-a-point decision. Variance 0 on the two Grand Plaza lists, where the win-on-the-spot (+0.5) offsets the Legend's draw (-0.5), and -0.5 on total's list for the Legend's draw. Cards that decided each Axis. Pace: Spiderling at 3 cost with 1 printed Might and no cards costing 5+ beyond Vilemaw in tachu's list. Stance: one growing body against a dozen-plus counters. Complexity: 20 hidden engine copies, so the formula counts each as a moving part. Variance: the engine tag counts heavily, plus Invert Timelines, Double Trouble and Grand Plaza. Legend ability: when you or an ally hold, you may exhaust Vex, Gloomist to draw 1. Also played: none. Confidence: medium. Reviewer check: the picks' rater found the formula's Complexity 3.5 to 4 above judgment and its Variance up to 2 above. It counts 20 copies of one card as 20 separate moving parts and swings, when the deck is really one of the most consistent here. The final 8 and 5.5 may overstate how hard and how swingy it is to pilot. The fetched tachu page showed no guide text (the section was empty on fetch), so the guide the picks describe was not re-read. The howItPlays line about Flurry of Feathers applies to MipZ's list; not every Spiderling list runs it.
